title: Siam Park Tenerife: Rides, Attractions & Must-Try Experiences
metaTitle: Siam Park Tenerife Rides: Slides, Attractions & Guide
metaDescription: Discover the best Siam Park Tenerife rides and water slides. Complete guide to Tower of Power, Singha, Wave Palace, height restrictions, and visitor tips.
excerpt: Explore the best Siam Park Tenerife rides, from the Tower of Power and Singha to lazy rivers, wave pools, height rules, and queue-busting tips.
quickAnswer: Siam Park Tenerife rides cater to every thrill level, ranging from the adrenaline-fueled Tower of Power (28m vertical drop through a shark aquarium) and Singha water coaster to the 3-meter waves at Wave Palace and the 1-kilometer Mai Thai River. Most thrill flumes require a minimum height of 1.25m, while Tower of Power requires 1.40m and 14 years of age.
imageAlt: Siam Park Tenerife water slides and swimming pools surrounded by tropical palms
content:
Perched along the sunny hills of Costa Adeje in southern Tenerife, Siam Park is celebrated globally as one of the world’s finest aquatic theme parks. Designed with authentic Thai architecture and lush tropical greenery, the park offers an exceptional variety of aquatic adventures. From sheer vertical drop flumes to tranquil lagoon loops, experiencing the iconic Siam Park Tenerife rides is a highlight of any Canary Islands holiday.

Whether you are chasing heart-pounding adrenaline, planning a family outing with children, or looking to unwind along warm white sand beaches, understanding how attractions are organized helps you make the most of your visit. This comprehensive guide details the best rides at Siam Park, official height restrictions, family areas, and practical tips to beat the queues.

Rope-Drop Ride Strategy

Head straight to high-demand thrill flumes like Tower of Power, Singha, and Saifa during the first 90 minutes after opening at 10:00 AM. Tour buses arrive between 11:30 AM and 1:00 PM, making mornings and late afternoons the fastest times to ride.

Top Thrill Water Slides at Siam Park

For thrill-seekers, Siam Park delivers world-class engineering and record-breaking drops. The park’s adrenaline collection features steep freefalls, water-propulsion coasters, and immense zero-gravity funnels.

Tower of Power

The flagship attraction of Siam Park is the Tower of Power. Riders climb a 28-meter (92-foot) Thai temple tower before plunging down an almost vertical open-air drop. Reaching speeds up to 80 km/h (50 mph), the slide shoots you through a transparent acrylic tunnel surrounded by a shark and ray aquarium. Minimum height is 1.40 meters, and riders must be at least 14 years old.

Singha & Saifa: High-Speed Water Coasters

Unlike conventional flumes, Singha is a hybrid water roller coaster. High-pressure water jets propel three-person inline rafts uphill at speeds up to 18 m/s (65 km/h) through 14 sharp turns. Saifa is the park’s newest double-lane dueling coaster, launching two-person rafts side-by-side along parallel 306-meter tracks. Both coasters require a minimum height of 1.25 meters.

The Dragon & Kinnaree

Group slides offer shared excitement. The Dragon seats four riders in a cloverleaf raft that drops into a 20-meter-wide open funnel, oscillating up vertical walls under a giant dragon sculpture. Kinnaree stretches 213 meters through hillside greenery, combining an enclosed funnel, an abrupt drop, and a tornado wall turn before splashing down (minimum height: 1.25 meters).

Vulcano

Carrying four riders on a round tube, Vulcano plunges into pitch-black darkness inside an artificial volcano. Synchronized lasers and volcanic sound effects create a sensory descent before returning to daylight.

Family Rides and Relaxation Attractions

Beyond extreme freefalls, a wide selection of Siam Park attractions caters to families and guests seeking moderate adventures or scenic leisure.

Mekong Rapids & Naga Racer

Mekong Rapids simulates a white-water expedition for four to five riders in circular rafts (minimum height: 1.10 meters). For friendly competition, Naga Racer features six parallel lanes where riders dive head-first on cushioned foam mats through undulating straightaways with speed sensor timers.

The Wave Palace & Siam Beach

The centerpiece of the relaxation zone is The Wave Palace, an immense heated lagoon flanked by 330 meters of natural white sand. It generates artificial surf waves up to 3 meters high—the largest in any water park worldwide. Swimmers can ride rolling swells in the deep zone or wade along the gentle shoreline.

Mai Thai River

Stretching over one kilometer, the Mai Thai River is one of the world’s longest lazy rivers. Drifting on inflatable rings past waterfalls and exotic greenery, guests can choose a gentle circuit or take an automated lift to a slide that passes through a shark aquarium.

Children’s Areas: The Lost City & Sawasdee

Families with younger children enjoy dedicated, safe aquatic zones:

  • The Lost City: An interactive fortress with 15 child-sized slides, climbing nets, water cannons, and shallow heated pools.
  • Sawasdee: Scaled-down replicas of famous thrill rides, allowing kids under 1.25 meters to enjoy gentle Siam Park water slides.

Siam Park Rides & Height Requirements

Attraction Thrill Level Min Height Ride Format
Tower of Power Extreme 1.40 m (14+ yrs) Single body slide
Singha & Saifa High 1.25 m Water coaster rafts
The Dragon & Kinnaree High 1.25 m 4-person group rafts
Mekong Rapids Medium 1.10 m Family circular raft
Naga Racer Medium 1.10 m 6-lane mat racer
The Wave Palace Moderate No minimum Wave pool & beach
Mai Thai River Relaxing No minimum 1 km lazy river loop

Practical Tips for Planning Your Day

  • Book tickets in advance: Purchasing online lets you scan mobile barcodes and skip morning box-office queues.
  • Wear neoprene water shoes: Paved paths warm up under the sun. Shoes are permitted on almost all slides.
  • Rent a locker early: Secure belongings upon arrival near the main entrance or Siam Beach.
  • Consider the All-Inclusive ticket: Bundles priority Fast Track, lunch, drinks, lockers, and towels for busy visits.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the scariest ride at Siam Park?

Most visitors consider the Tower of Power the scariest attraction due to its 28-meter near-vertical drop and aquarium tunnel. The high-speed water coasters Singha and Saifa offer the greatest speed and acceleration.

Are all rides included in general admission?

Yes. General admission includes unlimited access to all slides, the Wave Palace, lazy river, and children’s zones all day. Fast Track and lockers are optional upgrades unless booking an all-inclusive pass.

Are the pools and slides heated?

Yes. All water across Siam Park is heated to 24°C (75°F) year-round, ensuring comfortable conditions in every season.

What is the minimum height for major slides?

Most major adrenaline slides require a height of 1.25 meters (4 ft 1 in). Mekong Rapids and Naga Racer require 1.10 meters (3 ft 7 in), while the Tower of Power requires 1.40 meters (4 ft 7 in) and an age of at least 14.

title: Best Time of Year to Visit Siam Park: Seasons, Water Temps & Crowds
metaTitle: Best Time of Year to Visit Siam Park (Seasons, Weather & Crowds)
metaDescription: Discover the best time of year to visit Siam Park in Tenerife. Learn about heated water temps, quiet shoulder months, summer rush, and opening hour tips.
excerpt: From warm spring days to winter visits with 24°C heated water, discover the best months and hours to experience Siam Park with minimal queues.
quickAnswer: The best time of year to visit Siam Park is during the shoulder months of May, June, September, and October. Arriving at 9:30 AM before the 10:00 AM opening allows you to ride headline slides like Tower of Power and Singha with virtually no waiting before tour groups arrive.
imageAlt: Siam Park Tenerife water slide tower with turquoise water pools and tropical palms
content:
Planning a trip to Tenerife’s premier Thai-themed water park requires smart scheduling. Understanding the best time to visit Siam Park can transform your day from waiting in hour-long queues to breezing through world-class flumes and lounging along white sand lagoons.

Ideal Seasons: Shoulder Months vs. Peak Summer

Siam Park enjoys south Tenerife’s reliable subtropical sunshine throughout the entire calendar year. However, guest volumes fluctuate dramatically depending on European holiday calendars and seasonal weather patterns.

Spring & Autumn Sweet Spot (May–June & September–October)

For the ultimate balance of warm Atlantic sunshine and manageable queue times, late spring (May to June) and early autumn (September to October) are undeniably the prime windows. Daily temperatures hover pleasantly between 24°C and 28°C, ideal for water slides and sunbathing. Because primary European school terms are active during these periods, ride wait times rarely exceed 15 to 20 minutes outside of weekend afternoons.

Summer Rush (July & August)

July and August represent the busiest months of the year. Daily temperatures frequently top 30°C, drawing massive family crowds and vacation groups. Popular thrill rides such as the Tower of Power, Singha, and Kinnaree can see waits stretching past 60 to 75 minutes by midday. If your only window coincides with peak summer, buying tickets online in advance and investing in a Fast Track pass is virtually mandatory to maximize your slide count.

Winter Visiting & Heated Water Temperatures (November–April)

Visiting during winter offers remarkably quiet park grounds. A common concern is water temperature, but Siam Park utilizes an eco-friendly heating system that warms all pool and slide water to a comfortable 24°C (75°F) year-round. While ambient air temperatures can feel cool when exiting rides on breezy January afternoons, queue times drop to negligible levels, allowing you to walk directly onto headline attractions.

Best Time of Day & Opening Rope-Drop Strategy

Arriving early is the single most effective tactic for any Siam Park visit. The park gates open promptly at 10:00 AM daily. Aim to reach the entrance turnstiles by 09:30 AM to clear security checks, rent your locker, and position yourself before the main rush.

Morning Rush vs. Afternoon Lull

Tour buses and resort excursions typically arrive between 11:30 AM and 1:00 PM, creating peak congestion until mid-afternoon. Ride headline attractions—Tower of Power, Dragon, and Mekong Rapids—during the first 90 minutes. When lines peak midday, drift along the tranquil Mai Thai River, catch artificial swells at the Wave Palace, or grab lunch. Queues taper off again during the final two hours before closing.

Best Days of the Week to Avoid Crowds

Tuesdays and Wednesdays are statistically the quietest days at Siam Park. Many holidaymakers arrive in Tenerife on weekends or Mondays, saving major theme park visits for Thursday through Sunday. Local residents also flock to the park on Saturdays and Sundays, making midweek visits far smoother.

Essential Tips for a Smooth Visit

  • Book tickets online in advance: Skip the morning box-office queue and head straight to barcode turnstiles.
  • Wear neoprene water shoes: Dark concrete paths heat up under the Canary Island sun, and water shoes can be worn on most slides.
  • Rent a locker immediately: Lockers near the entrance fill rapidly; secure one first thing to stow dry clothes and valuables.
  • Consider the All-Inclusive ticket: Bundles priority fast track, lunch, lockers, and towels, proving high value in high season.

By timing your arrival for 09:30 AM on a midweek shoulder-season morning, you will experience the best time to visit Siam Park with minimal queues, perfect sunshine, and maximum thrills.

content:
Siam Park Tickets: Prices, What’s Included & Visitor Tips

Planning a visit to Siam Park in Tenerife? Famous for its Thai-inspired design, tropical scenery, giant artificial waves, and thrilling water slides, Siam Park is one of the island’s most popular attractions. Whether you are travelling as a couple, visiting with friends, or planning a family day out, choosing the right ticket can help you make the most of your visit.

However, not all Siam Park tickets offer the same benefits. Some options focus on park admission, while others may include food, drinks, lockers, towels, or additional experiences. Understanding these differences before booking can help you choose an option that fits your budget and plans.

This guide covers Siam Park ticket options, what to check before purchasing, the park’s top attractions, and practical tips for planning your day.

Which Siam Park Ticket Should You Choose?

The best Siam Park ticket depends on how you want to experience the park and which extras matter to you.

Standard admission tickets

A standard admission ticket is a straightforward option if you want access to the park’s attractions without paying for a package of additional services.

This option may suit visitors who plan to purchase food and drinks separately, bring their own suitable essentials, and spend most of their time enjoying the rides and pools.

Check the current admission conditions carefully, including whether any specific services or facilities require separate payment.

All-inclusive ticket options

If you want to simplify your spending during the day, compare any available all-inclusive ticket options.

Depending on the package offered, extras may include food, drinks, lockers, towels, or other services. Inclusions can vary, so read the exact package description before booking.

An all-inclusive option may be convenient for visitors who expect to spend a full day at the park and use the included services.

Combined attraction tickets

Some ticket options combine Siam Park admission with another attraction, such as Loro Parque on Tenerife's northern coast.

A combined ticket may be worth considering if you want to visit both parks during your trip. However, plan your transport and schedule carefully because the attractions are in different parts of the island.

Confirm the validity period, entry requirements, and whether you need to reserve visits separately.

Siam Park Ticket Prices: What Should You Expect?

Siam Park ticket prices depend on the ticket category, package inclusions, visitor eligibility, and any current offers.

Rather than relying on an old price list, check the official ticket page for the latest rates before purchasing.

When comparing tickets, look at these details:

  • Admission: Does the ticket cover entry to Siam Park on your intended visit date?

  • Food and drinks: Are refreshments included, and are there restrictions on what you can order?

  • Lockers and towels: Are these included in the package or charged separately?

  • Additional services: Check whether fast-track access or other extras are available and included.

  • Validity: Confirm whether the ticket is valid for one visit, multiple visits, or a specified period.

  • Transport: Determine whether getting to the park is your responsibility or part of a package.

The cheapest ticket is not always the best value. Compare the total cost of the admission ticket and the extras you expect to use.

Best Rides and Attractions at Siam Park

Siam Park offers a mix of high-adrenaline slides, relaxing waterways, wave pools, and family-friendly areas. Your priorities will depend on your age, interests, and comfort with water rides.

Tower of Power

Tower of Power is one of Siam Park’s most recognisable attractions. Its steep, high-speed drop makes it a favourite for thrill-seekers.

Check the posted height, health, and other ride requirements before joining the queue.

Dragon

Dragon combines a large funnel-shaped structure with a dramatic raft ride. It is a popular choice for groups looking for an exciting water attraction.

Review the ride restrictions and follow staff instructions before boarding.

Wave Palace

Wave Palace is famous for its large artificial waves and beach-style setting. It is an excellent place to take a break from slides while enjoying the park’s tropical atmosphere.

Wave sessions and swimming conditions are subject to park operations and safety instructions.

Mai Thai River

Mai Thai River offers a more relaxed experience, allowing visitors to float through tropical surroundings.

It can be a welcome change of pace between more intense rides. Follow the park’s guidance on suitable sections and access restrictions.

The Lost City

The Lost City is a water-play area designed especially for younger visitors, with interactive features and smaller slides.

Families should check the current age, height, and supervision requirements before visiting.

When Is the Best Time to Visit Siam Park?

Tenerife enjoys a mild climate throughout much of the year, making Siam Park an appealing attraction in different seasons. Nevertheless, weather, school holidays, and visitor demand can affect your experience.

Visit early in the day

Arriving near opening time gives you more flexibility to explore popular attractions before the busiest periods develop.

Check the official opening hours for your date and allow enough time to park, enter, and organise your belongings.

Consider weekdays

If your travel dates are flexible, compare weekday and weekend options outside major school holidays. Crowds vary, and no particular day is guaranteed to be quiet, but avoiding peak travel periods may make planning easier.

Check seasonal opening hours

Opening times and operating schedules can change. Before travelling, confirm the park’s calendar and check whether any attractions have planned maintenance or temporary closures.

How to Get to Siam Park

Siam Park is located in Costa Adeje in southern Tenerife, making it convenient for visitors staying around Playa de las Américas, Los Cristianos, and nearby resorts.

From Costa Adeje

If you are staying nearby, a taxi or local transport may be a convenient way to reach the entrance. Check the journey time from your accommodation before setting off.

From Playa de las Américas or Los Cristianos

These popular resort areas are relatively close to Siam Park. Depending on your location, you may be able to use local transport, a taxi, or a park transfer service if one is available.

From Tenerife South Airport

Visitors arriving at Tenerife South Airport can travel to the park by taxi, rental car, or suitable public transport connections. Allow extra time if you are travelling directly from the airport, particularly if you have luggage.

Check transport availability, routes, and prices for your travel date rather than assuming a transfer is included with your ticket.

What Should You Bring to Siam Park?

A little preparation can make a full day at a water park more comfortable.

  • Swimwear: Wear suitable swimwear and review any attraction-specific clothing rules.

  • Sun protection: Bring appropriate sunscreen and reapply it according to its instructions.

  • Waterproof essentials: Protect your phone and other valuables from water.

  • Footwear: Bring suitable footwear for walking around the park, checking the rules for where it can be worn.

  • Towel and change of clothes: Check whether towels are included in your ticket package.

  • Payment method: Bring an accepted payment method for any extras not covered by your ticket.

  • Booking confirmation: Keep your ticket or booking confirmation accessible at the entrance.

Check the park's current rules on outside food, personal belongings, lockers, and other items before your visit.

Is Siam Park Worth Visiting?

Siam Park can be an excellent choice if you enjoy water slides, tropical settings, wave pools, and a mix of exciting and relaxing attractions.

It is particularly appealing to visitors who want to dedicate a substantial part of their Tenerife holiday to a water park. Families, couples, and groups can all find attractions suited to different interests, although individual ride restrictions apply.

To decide whether it fits your trip, consider the admission cost, the amount of time you have available, your interest in water attractions, and the additional expenses you may incur inside the park.

Booking in advance can help you understand your options and organise your day, but always read the terms attached to the specific ticket you select.

Frequently Asked Questions About Siam Park Tickets

Should I buy Siam Park tickets in advance?

Booking ahead is a sensible way to organise your visit and check the available ticket options. Availability and booking requirements depend on the date and ticket type, so confirm the current conditions through the official website.

Does a Siam Park ticket include food and drinks?

Not every ticket includes food and drinks. Check whether your selected option is standard admission or a package that includes refreshments, and review any applicable limitations.

How long should I spend at Siam Park?

Many visitors set aside most of a day to enjoy the park's main attractions, take breaks, and explore at a comfortable pace. Your ideal visit length depends on queues, operating hours, and the number of rides you want to experience.

Is Siam Park suitable for children?

Siam Park has areas designed for younger visitors as well as attractions aimed at thrill-seekers. Check individual ride restrictions, supervision requirements, and height limits before your visit.

Can I visit Siam Park and Loro Parque on the same ticket?

Combined ticket options may be available. Check the current package details, validity period, entry rules, and the time needed to travel between the parks before booking.

What should I check before booking Siam Park tickets?

Compare admission, inclusions, validity, opening hours, ride restrictions, cancellation terms, and any additional charges. Use the official Siam Park website to confirm the latest details.

Plan Your Siam Park Visit

A successful day at Siam Park starts with choosing a ticket that matches your plans. Whether you want to experience the Tower of Power, enjoy the Wave Palace, float along the Mai Thai River, or spend time with family in the water-play areas, understanding your ticket options helps you plan with confidence.

Compare available Siam Park tickets before you travel, check the current operating information, and arrive prepared for a full day of water-based fun in Tenerife.

title: How to Get to Siam Park: Transport, Opening Hours & What to Pack

metaDescription: Complete transport and planning guide for Siam Park in Tenerife. Shuttle bus routes, opening hours, and an essential packing checklist.
excerpt: Getting to Siam Park Siam Park sits right in Costa Adeje on Tenerife's south coast. Many hotels in Costa Adeje are within easy walking distance or a short free shuttle ride, while a free Siam Park…
quickAnswer: Siam Park is in Costa Adeje, Tenerife. A free shuttle bus runs from many hotels in Costa Adeje, Los Cristianos, and Las Américas, and public TITSA buses and taxis also serve the park directly.
imageAlt: A resort coastline in Tenerife near Costa Adeje
content:
Getting to Siam Park

Siam Park sits right in Costa Adeje on Tenerife's south coast. Many hotels in Costa Adeje are within easy walking distance or a short free shuttle ride, while a free Siam Park shuttle bus also serves hotels in Los Cristianos and Las Américas. Elsewhere on the island, public TITSA buses and taxis serve the park directly, and paid parking is available on-site.

Opening Hours by Season

In summer season (May 1 to October 29), Siam Park is open 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM daily. In winter season (October 30 to April 30), it's open 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM daily. The park is closed on December 25 and January 1, and last entry is typically 1 hour before closing.

Essential Packing Checklist

  • Swimwear (worn under your clothes saves a locker trip)

  • Reef-safe sunscreen and a hat or rash vest for sun protection

  • A towel, unless your ticket already includes one

  • A dry bag or waterproof phone pouch for the wave and river rides

  • A change of clothes for the journey home

Make the Most of Your Day

Arrive right at opening, hit the headline slides first, and take a relaxed float down Mai Thai River once the midday crowds build up. If you're staying in Tenerife for more than a day, pair your visit with a trip to Loro Parque using the Twin Ticket.

title: General Admission vs. All-Inclusive: Which Siam Park Ticket Should You Book?
metaTitle: Siam Park General Admission vs All-Inclusive: Honest Comparison (2026)
metaDescription: Comparing Siam Park's General Admission ticket vs the All-Inclusive ticket: cost breakdown, what's included, and which is worth it.
excerpt: A transparent comparison between Siam Park's standard General Admission ticket and the All-Inclusive ticket with Fast Track, food and drinks.
quickAnswer: If you're visiting on a quieter day or don't mind occasional queues, General Admission is the better value. If you're visiting in peak season or want to maximize ride time, the All-Inclusive ticket's Fast Track pass usually pays for itself.
imageAlt: A tropical water slide tower at a Thai-inspired water park
content:
When booking your Siam Park visit, one of the first decisions is whether to go with the standard General Admission ticket or upgrade to the All-Inclusive ticket.

Why the All-Inclusive Ticket Wins in Peak Season

The All-Inclusive ticket bundles a Fast Track pass — one priority ride per participating slide — with lunch, drinks, a towel and a locker. In July and August, when queues at Tower of Power and Wave Palace can run long, Fast Track alone can save you well over an hour of standing in line.

When General Admission Makes More Sense

On a quieter weekday, in shoulder season, or if you're happy to bring your own towel and buy food as you go, General Admission covers everything you actually need — full-day access to every ride — at the lowest price.

The Verdict

Book the All-Inclusive ticket if you're visiting in peak season or want a stress-free day with lunch, drinks and Fast Track sorted in advance. Book General Admission if you're visiting off-peak or prefer to keep things simple and pay as you go.

title: Best Time to Visit Siam Park: Weather, Crowds & Queue Tips
metaTitle: Best Time to Visit Siam Park (2026 Guide: Avoid Crowds & Queues)
metaDescription: Discover the best time of day and month to visit Siam Park. Expert tips on avoiding crowds, queues at Tower of Power, and getting the most rides in.
excerpt: Opening vs. midday, best months for shorter queues at Tower of Power, and why arriving right at opening completely changes your day.
quickAnswer: Arrive right at 10:00 AM opening time and head straight for Tower of Power. You'll get short or no queues on the park's most popular slide before the crowds build up around midday.
imageAlt: Sunlight over a water park slide tower in the early morning
content:
Siam Park is consistently ranked among the world's best water parks, which means it can also get busy — especially in peak summer season. The timing of your visit makes a real difference to how many rides you can fit in.

The Golden Rule: Opening Rush vs. Midday Crowds

Siam Park opens at 10:00 AM daily. Guests who arrive right at opening and head straight for Tower of Power or Wave Palace get noticeably shorter queues than those who arrive after 11:30 AM, once coach groups and later arrivals fill the park.

Best Months of the Year to Visit

Tenerife's climate is mild year-round, but Siam Park is busiest in July and August, and around Spanish and UK school holiday weeks. Late spring (May–June) and early autumn (September–October) offer warm weather with noticeably thinner crowds.

Weekday vs. Weekend

Weekdays outside school holidays are consistently quieter than weekends, when local visitors join the usual tourist crowd. If your schedule is flexible, a Tuesday or Wednesday visit is a good bet.

Summary & Recommendations

To get the most out of your visit, book online in advance, arrive right at 10:00 AM, and hit the park's most popular slides — Tower of Power and Wave Palace — first, before working your way to the more relaxed Mai Thai River later in the day.
